answer: Coordinated-Action Pricing. Each agent gets a unique graph vertex; a new identity must acquire a scarcity slot via a market priced by current coordination depth. Slot price rises with the number of distinct vertices already transacting in the same grove (functional cluster), so spawning N cheap identities forces the attacker to pay escalating marginal prices per slot. A velocity ledge caps how fast one actor can occupy adjacent vertices. Cost: linear-plus-convex slot outlay scaled to grove density, making mass sybils economically dominated.
